title: What the Body Still Carries
logline: As an elder's hearing fades, a household finds new ways to reach her, and everyone relearns together how she now takes in the world.
human_question: When one of the senses weakens, how does a person's whole way of taking the world in, and a family's way of reaching them, actually change?

situation.what_happens: In a household of several generations, an elder's hearing has been going for years. Nobody announced it and nobody made a plan. Instead the household has quietly rebuilt its habits around it: people turn to face her before speaking, a grandchild writes things down, the loudest room is avoided, jokes are repeated once and then let go. Some of this works and some of it fails, and the failures are ordinary and often funny. She has her own view of how much of it she needs, and it does not always match theirs.
situation.who_is_involved: The elder, whose consent is the first and most important one and is separate from the family's; the adult children who carry most of the adaptation; the grandchildren, who learn it as normal and do it best; and neighbours and workmates who do not adapt at all, which is part of the story.
situation.what_is_at_stake: For the elder, how much of the household's life she is still inside, and whether the help offered is help or management. For the family, the work of adapting and the tiredness in it that nobody says out loud. For the film, her dignity, which comes before every other consideration in it.
situation.how_it_unfolds: A change like this has no beginning that anyone can name and no ending. The pressures are money, the household's other demands, and the difference between what she wants and what her family thinks she needs. It ends where the film stops, not where the situation does, and it should say so.

concept_merge.why_together: C037 contributes the claim that for beings with both mind and body no mental event floats free: each one rests on a particular piece of living matter, and when the body changes, what the mind can do changes with it. C035 contributes the precision that makes this about a threshold rather than an ear, since the door is a fine sensitivity inside the organ and not the organ itself, and experience gets in only where something strikes that sensitivity strongly enough. C048 contributes what is lost further downstream: the sources list hearing what others say among the ordinary things that set a person's inner life going at all, so a narrowing channel is not only a loss of information. Together they describe what a household is actually rebuilding.
concept_merge.what_it_reveals: Separately these are a classification of bases and doors. Together, in a household, they show that adapting to a sense that has weakened is not a matter of volume but of rebuilding the routes by which anything reaches anyone at all, and that a family doing this without being asked has worked out the same structure the sources set out. The film's honesty depends on holding one line firmly: the sources' own statements about faculties and rebirth are about doctrine and must never be turned toward the person in the room.

concept_links.why: The digest holds that mental life, for beings like us, always depends on a physical base, a working sense sensitivity for each sense and a further base for most other mental activity [C037-P:L27], and says in plain words that when the body changes, what the mind can do changes with it. The digest's own story seed for this concept is a family finding new ways to reach an elder who has gradually lost their hearing. Two prohibitions from the digest are load-bearing here and are written into the film rather than left implied: the source's phrase 'beings with complete faculties' must never become a judgement about disabled people, and Margaya's claim that the first stage of awakening depends on hearing another person is a doctrinal point about the formless realms and must never be presented as saying that deaf or hard-of-hearing people are spiritually disadvantaged. The heart-base is likewise not cardiology and not 'follow your heart'.

The digest separates the visible organ from the fine sensitivity inside it, and says experience only gets in where something strikes that sensitivity strongly enough to interrupt the resting mind, so having eyes open is not yet seeing. That frames hearing loss as a threshold rather than a broken part, which is closer to how the household actually deals with it. The digest's limit applies: the sensitivity is not the eardrum or nerve endings, and the traditional descriptions of it are not anatomy.

The digest lists the ordinary things the source says set mind-door processes going: sense contact, hearing what others say, reading, a question put to us, thinking, hunger and thirst, bodily pain, meeting friends or enemies [C048-M:L5]. The digest's own gloss is that the inner life is seldom self-starting and is prompted from outside by people and words. Watching a household invent new prompts when one of those channels narrows is that claim from the other side. The digest notes the source's list is explicitly only a portion of the causes, so the film does not present it as complete.

what_the_viewer_could_understand: These texts say that for beings with a body, every moment of mind rests on a piece of living matter, and that what reaches us at all depends on a fine threshold inside the organ rather than the organ we can point to. A household quietly rebuilding how it reaches one of its own is that structure being handled by people who have never read a word of it.
what_must_be_real: The elder's own clear, separate and ongoing consent, which outranks the family's and may be withdrawn at any point, including after filming. No framing may turn her hearing loss into a moral lesson, and no part of the sources' teaching about faculties, rebirth or spiritual capacity may be brought anywhere near her.
position_hint: held rather than placed: it belongs beside the group's film about several senses working together, as its counterpart, and would sit wherever that film sits if a slot opened.
risks: Pity-framing a vulnerable elder instead of showing her own agency and her own view of what she needs.
The family's consent being allowed to stand in for hers.
Any implication of a link between hearing loss and the sources' doctrinal claims about faculties or spiritual capacity, which the C037 and C009 digests both forbid.
Turning a household's ordinary adaptation into an inspirational arc.
Filming a household over months and leaving them with the consequences of a broadcast.
drop_if: The elder does not clearly and separately consent, even if the family agrees.
The family does not want their adaptation shown.
The story cannot be told without exploiting a vulnerable person's condition.
The doctrinal frame cannot be kept entirely away from the person on screen.

connections.note: Both study the senses at work, one where several combine in a skilled trade and one where a household adapts as one of them weakens.
Both are about a threshold below which nothing arrives, one at the edge of a lamp's reach and one inside a person's own hearing.

selection.reason: Strong and proposed by the C037 and C045 digests' own story seeds, but the group's twelve slots are filled, and its concept ground is already carried live by other films. Held rather than folded into a kept idea, because a real person's hearing loss should not be carried into a film whose doctrinal frame the digests prohibit applying to it.

unknowns: No participant or event has been found or confirmed. Everything here is a research direction.
evidence_class_note: Editorial proposal. No location, scene or shot decisions are made at the idea stage.
